issues.description: Unbounded log buffer can leak memory if crash never occurs and recording disabled
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler.buffer grows without limit until init_recording is called or job exits. If a job runs for a long time with server-side recording disabled, every root log record is retained until _stop_log_buffering fires. Consider a ring buffer or size/time cap, since crash logs only need the recent tail.

issues.description: Removing all OTLP LoggingHandlers in _shutdown_telemetry may strip handlers not owned by this provider
issues.detail: _shutdown_telemetry now iterates root handlers and removes every LoggingHandler instance before force_flush. If the host process attached its own OTLP LoggingHandler (or another provider's), it will be silently detached. Filter to only the handler associated with this logger_provider to avoid collateral damage.

issues.description: _on_cleanup crash-log path leaves buffer attached on success path without flushing
issues.detail: When init_recording is called from _on_cleanup with logs=True, it falls through to init_recording which now calls _stop_log_buffering early (if _recording_initialized) and returns. But on first call _recording_initialized is False, so it proceeds to setup and _flush_early_log_buffer(replay=True). However, the except branch calls _stop_log_buffering, dropping buffered crash logs — exactly the logs we wanted to upload.

issues.description: Replay through OTLP LoggingHandler may not find handler in time / race with setup
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer searches root handlers for a LoggingHandler immediately after init_recording's _setup_cloud_tracer. If _setup_cloud_tracer attaches asynchronously or under a different logger, the loop silently does nothing and buffered records are dropped. Worth asserting the handler was found and logging a warning otherwise.

issues.description: Removing -n auto and dropping test_plugin_google_stt.py from unit-tests reduces CI coverage
issues.detail: The makefile change disables pytest-xdist parallelism (slower CI) and removes tests/test_plugin_google_stt.py from the unit-tests target. No justification in the PR description for either. If the google STT test is flaky or the parallel mode caused issues, that should be documented; otherwise this looks like an accidental regression.

issues.description: process_closed emitted on init failure may surprise existing listeners
issues.detail: proc_pool now emits 'process_closed' when warmup initialization fails. Previously this event fired only after a process that had been monitored closed. Listeners that assume the process was ever live (e.g., accessing proc.pid, exitcode) may now see None — the test diff already had to guard pid. Document the new contract or use a distinct event.

review.summary: The PR's core idea — buffer logs early and replay through OTLP on crash — is sound, but several edges need attention. The biggest risks are an unbounded buffer in long-running jobs, _shutdown_telemetry removing OTLP handlers it doesn't own, and the cleanup-path exception branch discarding the very crash logs it was meant to upload. Replay also relies on a fragile handler-lookup that silently no-ops if not found. Unrelated makefile changes (disabling -n auto, dropping google STT tests) reduce CI coverage without explanation.
